Why is the sky blue? Why not purple, or white?
Good question. The answer is hiding inside sunlight.
Sunlight looks white, but it is really every colour mixed together.
Each colour travels as a wave. Red waves are long. Blue waves are short.
When sunlight hits the air, tiny gas molecules bounce the short blue waves all over the sky.
Blue light scatters almost six times more than red light.
Violet scatters even more. But the sun sends less violet, and our eyes are less sensitive to it.
So the sky is blue because the air scatters blue sunlight in every direction.
